answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. Frame it as a ledge on the forge, collected by the quill: the farm pays a ledge that grows with the size of its cluster, and the quill is the party that profits from the farm being found out.
